LESSON: RELIGIOUS

Grade: Grade 2
Subject: HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Utsav
Topic 7.1: Religious

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Religious. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: When do you celebrate (Festivals) Festivals the learner should be able to: celebration of: your birthday?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use appropriate Prakash Utsav (Gurpurabs) greetings while  The
2. appreciate festivals for Stavans, Shabads and bhajans in groups their role in promoting related to festivals peace and friendship 

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: RELIGIOUS
Subject: HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Religious helps you succeed in HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: RELIGIOUS
Study Religious like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Use appropriate Prakash Utsav (Gurpurabs) greetings while  The

What this means
In this part you learn to use appropriate Prakash Utsav (Gurpurabs) greetings while  The. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use appropriate Prakash Utsav (Gurpurabs) greetings while  The.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Religious” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use appropriate Prakash Utsav (Gurpurabs) greetings while  The. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate festivals for Stavans, Shabads and bhajans in groups their role in promoting related to festivals peace and friendship 

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate festivals for Stavans, Shabads and bhajans in groups their role in promoting related to festivals peace and friendship . You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate festivals for Stavans, Shabads and bhajans in groups their role in promoting related to festivals peace and friendship .
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Religious in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate festivals for Stavans, Shabads and bhajans in groups their role in promoting related to festivals peace and friendship . Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Religious is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Religious” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: use appropriate Prakash Utsav (Gurpurabs) greetings while  The)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Religious in your own words. (skill: appreciate festivals for Stavans, Shabads and bhajans in groups their role in promoting related to festivals peace and friendship )

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Religious to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: use appropriate Prakash Utsav (Gurpurabs) greetings while  The.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate festivals for Stavans, Shabads and bhajans in groups their role in promoting related to festivals peace and friendship .
4. Make one local Kenya example of Religious from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Religious: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 2 learner study Religious?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. When do you celebrate (Festivals) Festivals the learner should be able to: celebration of: your birthday?
2. What do you do to in celebrating Birthdays Ram Navmi, celebrate your birthday?
3. Why do we celebrate community bonding Buddha Jayanti Janamashtami?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Religious means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: use appropriate Prakash Utsav (Gurpurabs) greetings while  The.
5. Be able to: appreciate festivals for Stavans, Shabads and bhajans in groups their role in promoting related to festivals peace and friendship .
